The U.S. government and prominent technology companies have made a series of significant announcements, contracts, projects, and investments in quantum tech, drone tech, robotics, space tech, satellite communication, nuclear energy, and artificial intelligence in recent months. Simultaneously, new 2x leveraged single-stock Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) have launched or been filed for launch, providing amplified exposure to individual companies.

### Government and Industry Developments in Advanced Technologies

**Quantum Technology**
The U.S. government is heavily investing in quantum technology. The Department of Commerce announced $2.013 billion in federal incentives under the CHIPS and Science Act, including $375 million for GlobalFoundries to establish a secure domestic quantum foundry and $1 billion for IBM for a new quantum foundry subsidiary. Quantinuum and Rigetti also received planned funding.

The Department of Defense (DoD) launched a multi-phase initiative on June 23, 2026, to integrate mature quantum sensing and timing technologies into the Joint Force, committing up to $200 million within the next year to develop high-fidelity quantum electric field sensors, magnetometers, gravimeters, and tactical clocks. The DoD also released a strategy requiring all systems to support post-quantum cryptography or be phased out by the end of 2030, with enhanced standards adopted by the end of 2031.

The Department of Energy (DoE) established the "Quantum Genesis" initiative on June 23, 2026, aiming to deploy the world's first fault-tolerant, scientifically relevant quantum computing capability by 2028. This initiative will include a National Quantum Supercomputing User Facility. NASA, through its Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) and academic partners, is developing the first space-based quantum sensor for gravity measurements, scheduled for launch around 2030, and is also investing in quantum Rydberg radar technologies. The General Services Administration (GSA) is expanding its testing to evaluate quantum-resistant solutions for federal buildings and will host the 2026 Post-Quantum Cryptography Summit.

**Drone Technology**
The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) awarded 12 companies positions on a potential five-year, $1.5 billion contract for counter-unmanned aircraft systems (C-UAS) hardware, software, and services on August 3, 2026. Awardees include BAE Systems, CACI International, Dedrone Defense, D-Fend Solutions, Fortem Technologies, and Leidos, among others.

The White House advanced a $1.1 billion "Drone Dominance Program" on August 20, 2026, to acquire over 200,000 American-made lethal small unmanned aerial systems (UAS) by 2027, with a focus on building a domestic supply chain for drone components. The Office of Strategic Capital (OSC) committed up to $820 million to Performance Drone Works (PDW) on July 31, 2026, to boost U.S. production of drone, robotics, and autonomous systems technologies. Additionally, the Department of War launched a "Drone Marketplace" on August 14, 2026, to streamline the procurement of unmanned systems across all military domains. Safe Pro Group announced over $5 million in AI-powered drone threat-detection orders from the U.S. Army, Air Force, and defense prime contractors through early August 2026.

Alphabet's Wing, a drone delivery company, received FAA approval for commercial drone deliveries in the U.S. on April 26, 2026, and continues to expand its Wing Delivery Network. Amazon reportedly acquired Zurich-based robotics startup Rivr in March 2026 and AI-driven robotics startup Rightbot in January 2026 to enhance delivery operations with autonomous systems.

**Robotics**
NASA continues its long-standing commitment to robotics for space exploration, with JPL leading the development of rovers, landers, and advanced robots for planetary missions. NASA Ames Research Center is also developing mobile bipedal robot systems for large-scale structural assembly in space. The OSC's loan to Performance Drone Works also includes the expansion of robotics and autonomous systems production. Amazon's recent acquisitions of Rivr and Rightbot underscore the "Magnificent 7" company's push into AI-driven robotics for logistics.

**Space Technology and Satellite Communication**
The U.S. Space Force awarded AnySignal a contract on August 20, 2026, to demonstrate space-to-space communications capabilities and develop a resilient space data transport backbone. On August 18, 2026, Rocket Lab was onboarded into the U.S. Space Force's Space Data Network (SDN) Consortium and received $12 million in delivery orders to develop a secure, high-speed global satellite communications network for military operations. Viasat also selected Rocket Lab on August 17, 2026, to build a geosynchronous Earth orbit (GEO) satellite for the Protected Tactical SATCOM-Global (PTS-G) program. The Space Force also awarded Rocket Lab a $397 million contract on August 14, 2026, to develop "Flatellites" for airborne threat tracking under the Space-Based Airborne Moving Target Indicator (SB-AMTI) program. Integrate received a new Space Force contract on August 24, 2026, for its AI-enabled project management platform to integrate national security space systems. General Dynamics Mission Systems secured a $30.4 million task order on August 10, 2026, to modernize the Mobile User Objective Ground System. Torch Technologies Inc. was awarded a nearly $1 billion indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract on August 10, 2026, for aerospace research, development, test, and evaluation activities.

**Nuclear Energy**
The DoE is accelerating advanced nuclear technologies. On August 25, 2026, its National Reactor Innovation Center (NRIC) selected 13 new projects to participate in the "Nuclear Energy Launch Pad" initiative, fostering private industry development of advanced nuclear technologies, including reactor development and nuclear fuel cycle advancements. The DoE also granted X-energy up to $1 billion in additional federal funding on August 23, 2026, for its small modular reactor project with Dow in Texas, bringing total public support to $2.15 billion. The U.S. hosted the ministerial launch of the International Atomic Energy Agency's (IAEA) "Atomic Technologies Licensed for Applications at Sea (ATLAS)" initiative on August 26-27, 2026, to advance maritime nuclear technologies. Urenco USA broke ground on August 18, 2026, to expand its National Enrichment Facility, and LIS Technologies began site-preparation for its laser-based uranium enrichment headquarters on August 24, 2026. Atomic Canyon raised $7 million for an AI tool rollout at U.S. nuclear plants on August 25, 2026.

**Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Latest Innovative Technologies**
The DoD entered into new agreements on May 1, 2026, with eight leading AI developers—NVIDIA, OpenAI, SpaceX, Reflection, AWS, Microsoft, Oracle, and Google—to deploy their AI products in classified military networks via GenAI.mil. The DoD also awarded MORSECORP, INC a $27.7 million contract for AI and machine learning development on August 16, 2026, and Public Spend Forum, LLC a $40.3 million contract for AI-driven market intelligence. NASA awarded $30 million to university aeronautics projects, including a Stanford University initiative to develop machine-learning-enabled aircraft avionics, announced on August 20, 2026, and August 25, 2026. NASA is also pursuing AI research assistants.

Among the "Magnificent 7" companies, Meta released its Muse Glimmer open-weight multimodal AI model on August 10, 2026, and introduced Muse Code and Muse Spark 1.2 on August 5, 2026. Meta is reportedly preparing to unveil its consumer-focused AI agent, "Hatch," in the coming weeks, with its "Watermelon" AI model slated for October. Google released Gemini 3.7 Flash on August 22, 2026, just three weeks after 3.6.
